output.summary: KEP-5241 sets the policy that feature gates must be complete (functional, security, monitoring, testing requirements, and known issues resolved) before being enabled by default, and that the only valid GA criteria is resolving all issues and gaps identified as feedback during beta.
output.rationale: Feature gates enabled by default run in every production cluster, so incomplete features there add stability, performance, and security risk. Once a feature is on by default, other workloads rely on it, which makes later changes and disabling it costly. The KEP therefore moves the Beta and GA bar so that Beta must already include all requirements, leaving no significant change for the GA promotion.

alternatives.option: Keep existing Beta/GA criteria that allow incomplete features to be enabled by default
alternatives.why_not: The readme states that enabling incomplete features in production by default is irresponsible and that known-incomplete features bring additional stability, performance, and security issues.

alternatives.option: Jump directly to GA (locked-on) without field experience
alternatives.why_not: The readme says that making the jump to GA without actual field experience is irresponsible.

alternatives.option: Phase in larger features through one large gate
alternatives.why_not: The readme instead recommends phasing in larger features over time using separate feature gates.

evidence.quote: The only valid GA criteria are “all issues and gaps identified as feedback during beta are resolved”.
Enabling incomplete features in production Kubernetes clusters by default is irresponsible.
Promotion from Beta to GA must have no significant change for the release.
Phasing in larger features over time can be done by bringing separate feature gates
